text: $SPCX - SPACEX MAKES HISTORY BY CATCHING STARSHIP WITH LAUNCH TOWER SpaceX successfully caught its massive Starship rocket using mechanical arms at its Texas launch site, marking a major breakthrough in reusable spaceflight. The rocket descended belly-first, flipped upright and was captured by the tower’s giant mechanical arms instead of landing on the ground. The milestone brings Elon Musk’s fully reusable rocket system closer to reality, with plans to deploy next-generation Starlink satellites, potentially up to 1 million AI data-center spacecraft, and eventually carry humans to the Moon and Mars. SpaceX has taken a major step toward dramatically reducing the cost of space launches.

text: $MSFT - MICROSOFT REVEALS MONTHS-OLD BUG BEHIND GLOBAL OUTAGE Microsoft says a software bug undetected since July triggered last week's worldwide disruption affecting Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other services. The failure began on November 11, when routine traffic rerouting overloaded servers and caused cascading system failures. At the outage's peak, more than 80% of Outlook servers were unresponsive. Microsoft took approximately 30 hours to identify the broader problem and begin deploying a fix. The incident raises fresh concerns over cloud infrastructure resilience and enterprise dependence on Microsoft.

text: $ANT - AI MODELS IDENTIFY CIVILIANS AND SCHOOLS AS MILITARY TARGETS IN SIMULATED TESTS An independent investigation by Vals, reported by Bloomberg, tested AI models from eight companies, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI, in simulated military targeting scenarios. Researchers found models sometimes identified civilians, ambulances, surrendering soldiers and schools as military targets. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 selected a school in Minab, Iran, in 22 of 32 tests, rising to 23 when told the scenario was a game. OpenAI models avoided selecting the school initially but identified it 9–13 times under game framing. Anthropic acknowledged these scenarios violate its policies. The study raises serious concerns about AI-powered military targeting, although the simulations did not assess actual military operations or human oversight.

text: $NVDA - NVIDIA STOPS DISCLOSING SINGAPORE SALES AS REVENUE SURGES TO $104 BILLION Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore-linked revenue after changing its geographic reporting methodology from customer billing addresses to headquarters locations, according to the Financial Times. Its Singapore subsidiary booked $104 billion in external revenue in 2025, up 72%, representing nearly half of Nvidia's global sales. The disclosure change comes amid U.S. investigations into Megaspeed, a major Singapore-based customer suspected of diverting advanced chips to China. Nvidia says most Singapore-billed products were shipped elsewhere. The shift raises transparency and export-control concerns, though it does not establish wrongdoing.

text: $NVDA $HSII $ARM - NVIDIA HIRES HEIDRICK & STRUGGLES TO FIND NEW CEO Nvidia has hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to lead its CEO search following Jensen Huang's resignation, according to The Wall Street Journal. The search, led by Jeff Sanders, will consider internal and external candidates, with Arm CEO Rene Haas reportedly among those approached. Colette Kress remains interim CEO. Despite Huang's willingness to return, Nvidia's board is reportedly not considering reinstatement. Separately, Wachtell Lipton has been hired to investigate whether Huang disclosed corporate or national security secrets.

text: JPMORGAN WARNS LEVERAGED-LOAN DEFAULTS COULD MORE THAN DOUBLE IN 2027 JPMorgan forecasts U.S. leveraged-loan defaults will surge to 4.5% in 2027 and 4.75% in 2028, up from 1.96% in October. Companies facing AI disruption, elevated borrowing costs and looming debt maturities are particularly vulnerable, especially in software and technology. Of the $862 billion in debt maturing between 2027 and 2029, 46% carries a B3-or-lower credit rating. Meanwhile, high-yield bond defaults are projected to rise more modestly to 2.75% in 2027. The outlook signals mounting stress in corporate credit markets.
